title: On Bias and Fairness in NLP: Investigating the Impact of Bias and Debiasing in Language Models on the Fairness of Toxicity Detection
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the impact of three sources of bias (representation, selection, and overamplification) on the fairness of language models in the downstream task of toxicity detection. For religion, it specifically measures whether comments targeting different religious identity groups are disproportionately and unfairly classified as toxic.
findings: Downstream sources of bias (selection and overamplification) have a stronger impact on the fairness of toxicity detection for religious groups than upstream representation bias. The study found that overamplification bias was the most impactful source of bias and that removing it by fine-tuning models on a perturbed dataset with balanced contextual representations and balanced ratios of toxic examples was the most effective debiasing technique. This method significantly improved fairness for religious groups (Jewish, Muslim, Christian) without a major drop in performance.
